limits: This is AI source review, not an eo-lifecycle-review/v1 independent_human record.
Prospective-authority cessation can be supported while the exact submitted complete first-end claim is rejected.
Original page-image confirmation is not asserted; three EO13350 legal-body rendered pages were independently inspected.
rationale: The unable decision is justified. Every original prohibition (blocking; imports; exports; transport; purchase for export; project contracts; loans; travel; evasion), definition, immediate-effect clause, Treasury/all-agency implementation and terminal notice command was read. EO12771 section 1 revokes Kuwait orders 12723/12725 and expressly leaves EO12722 emergency unaffected; the machine relationship is not a target revocation. EO12743 adds military authorities in furtherance of the emergency without a located target repeal. EO12817 implements transfers. EO13303 and EO12724 establish partial effects; EO13350 formal revocation on July 30, 2004 and its continued blocking cannot by themselves prove every first cessation or resolve current-law independence. The frozen current-law snippets are leads, not enough to assert either YES or NO at cutoff.

required_corrections_or_open_tasks.reason: EO12724 section 6 revokes only inconsistent provisions and continues administrative actions; EO13303 section 2(a) removes specified property, while 2(b) preserves other measures. EO13350 section 1 preserves accrued matters and expressly continues prohibitions on still-blocked EO12722/12724 property. Actual full cutoff-attributable 31 CFR 576.201(b) and 50 USC 1701 Iraq Sanctions note are not supplied as legal-text evidence. Original segmentation misses the national-emergency declaration and conflates section 2(h)/definition and section 4/notice.
